---
title: "Where is the neutral point and the required CG?"
---


::: {#f809f31c .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
ENTRY_CEILING = 90.0
SOLVE_BUDGET = 15.0
PROBE_POOL = 150.0
PROBE_SPENT = 5.2

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

airplane = get_airplane()
op_point = asb.OperatingPoint(velocity=10, alpha=0)

aero_stab = asb.AeroBuildup(
    airplane=airplane,
    op_point=op_point
).run_with_stability_derivatives()

x_np = aero_stab['x_np'][0]
mac = airplane.wings[0].mean_aerodynamic_chord()
cg_x = x_np - 0.10 * mac
```
:::


::: {.hero}
[0\.267 m]{.hero-value}
[Required CG location]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** The X-Wing's neutral point sits at $x =$ [0\.274]{.key} m from the nose reference. For pitch stability, placing the center of gravity at a 10% static margin requires it to be located at $x =$ [0\.267]{.key} m.

::: {#cell-fig-three-view .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
axs = airplane.draw_three_view(show=False)
fig = axs[0, 0].figure
fig.set_size_inches(8, 8)

for ax in [axs[0, 0], axs[1, 0]]:
    ax.plot([x_np], [0], [0], 'ro', markersize=6, label="Neutral Point")
    ax.plot([cg_x], [0], [0], 'bo', markersize=6, label="Required CG")

axs[0, 0].legend(loc="upper right")
plt.show()
```
